name: Malinaltepec Me'phaa
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Weathers, Esther L. & Mark L. Weathers. 1984. A sketch of Malinaltepec Tlapanec Phonology. Ms. 18pp. (Suarez 1988 sketch was read: tone-only, no acento/stress statement found)

new_statements.quote: Tlapanec employs iambic feet aligned to the right edge of the prosodic word (Marlett and Weathers 2018: 23; Suárez 1983: 26). The acoustic correlate of accent in Tlapanec is still unclear. [...] In order to reflect the fact that the acoustic correlate of stress in Tlapanec is still unclear, we refer to syllables as either "weak" versus "strong", rather than "unstressed" versus "stressed" [...] Marlett and Weathers (2018: 23–24) remark that there is evidence that words and phrases are prosodically right-headed (whether this syllable has a short vowel or long vowel; thus, quantity-insensitive) [...] Some contrasts are maintained only in the final syllable of the prosodic word; this is the phonological correlate of accent.
new_statements.citation: Uchihara, Hiroto & Gregorio Tiburcio Cano. 2022 [online 2021]. Foot-based allomorphy in Tlapanec (Mè'phàà). Linguistics 60(1): 83-122. doi:10.1515/ling-2020-0108 (open access, CC-BY).
new_statements.locator: Sec. 2.2 'Tlapanec prosodic structure', p. 88 (PDF p. 6); secondary-accent statement Sec. 4, p. 100 (PDF p. 18)
new_statements.rule_in_words: The final syllable of the prosodic word is the strong (accented) syllable: quantity-insensitive iambic feet are built from the right edge, and only that syllable licenses contrastive vowel length, nasalization and contour tones. The language is tonal (3 level tones, 9 melodies) and the authors stress that the phonetic correlate of accent is still disputed (no clear stress per Marlett & Weathers 2018; onset-consonant lengthening per Carrasco 2012 and Cornelio Tiburcio 2022; tone-conditioned per Herrera Zendejas 2018).
new_statements.secondary_stress: p. 100: 'Tlapanec has been argued to employ quantity-insensitive iambic feet and aligns them at the right edge of the prosodic word, assigned iteratively from right to left (cf. Marlett and Weathers 2018).... the strong syllable is indicated with a raised vertical line, while secondary accent is indicated with a lowered vertical line.' Secondary accent on the strong syllable of each non-head foot; the final foot is the head foot. Feet are disyllabic, so stems are mono- or disyllabic and affixed words get iterative feet.
new_statements.exceptions: Acoustic correlate unclear; speakers have difficulty identifying the strong syllable; a few contour tones occur in non-final syllables; Herrera Zendejas 2018 claims a tone-conditioned position instead of fixed final.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain = the prosodic word ('the domain of accentuation, the domain of a minimality requirement, and the domain of some tonal processes', p. 100), i.e. stem plus affixes; compounds may not form one prosodic word (fn. 14). Marlett & Weathers 2018 say words and phrases alike are right-headed.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding source's data are from the Huehuetepec variety (community of Zilacayotitlán, mun. Atlamajalcingo del Monte), which Marlett & Weathers 2018 Table 1 place under ISO tcf as 'tlapaneco del este [Huehuetepec]' ([tcf-Zila]); Glottolog mali1285 = tcf, so it is the same language but not the Malinaltepec-town subvariety. The statement is explicitly grounded in Marlett & Weathers 2018 (genus-wide, sampling [tcf-CVil], [tcf-Tepe], [tcf-Zila]) and Suárez 1983:26 (Malinaltepec). The competing tone-conditioned claim (Herrera Zendejas 2018) is about Malinaltepec proper. The instrumental confirmation of final stress (Cornelio Tiburcio 2022) is from Ciénega del Sauce, an Acatepec-type variety (acat1239), not tcf.

sources.locator: Sec. 2.2 'Tlapanec prosodic structure', p. 88 (PDF p. 6); secondary-accent statement Sec. 4, p. 100 (PDF p. 18)
sources.note: Sec. 2.2 p. 88: quantity-insensitive iambic feet aligned to the right edge of the prosodic word, final syllable strong; acoustic correlate of accent unclear (M&W 2018 'no clear stress'; Carrasco 2012 onset-consonant duration; Herrera 2018 tone-conditioned); phonological correlates = nasalization, vowel length and contour tones only in final syllable. Sec. 4 p. 100: feet assigned iteratively right-to-left, secondary accent on non-head feet; prosodic word = domain of accentuation. Data: Huehuetepec variety, Zilacayotitlan ([tcf-Zila]).

sources.citation: Navarro Solano, Abad. 2012. El patrón de alineamiento en el meʔ¹phaa¹ de Malinaltepec, Guerrero. MA thesis, CIESAS. 216 PDF pp.
sources.note: Ch. 3 phonology; sec. 3.3 pp. 30-31: prosodic word requires a bimoraic foot; long/laryngealized vowels only in monosyllables and the final syllable; sec. 3.4 tones (3 level + 6 contour, with F0 measurements). No acento/prominence statement (only 'acento' hits are about Carrasco's tone diacritics).

sources.citation: Cornelio Tiburcio, Oscar. 2022. El acento y la estructura prosódica en el mè'phàà de la Ciénega del Sauce, Guerrero. MA thesis, CIESAS. 235 pp.
sources.note: Instrumental study on an Acatepec-type variety (not tcf): stress fixed on the final syllable of the phonological word, only reliable correlate = onset-consonant duration (ch. 5, pp. 148-149); ch. 1 pp. 3-4 summarises the Malinaltepec hypotheses: Marlett & Weathers 2012/2018 and Carrasco 2012 ms. (fixed final) vs Herrera Zendejas 2018 (accent on the right-most highest tone).

sources.citation: Marlett, Stephen A. & Mark L. Weathers. 2018. The sounds of Me'phaa (Tlapanec): A new assessment. SIL-Mexico Electronic Working Papers 25. 31 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 7 'Prominence' pp. 23-24: 'It is not clear whether something comparable to stress is appropriately identified in Me'phaa. However, there is evidence that words and phrases are prosodically right-headed... In a disyllabic root, the final syllable is strong and the first is weak.' Cites Rensch 1978 'tonic ultima' and Suárez (1983:26) for final-syllable accent at an earlier stage. Genus-wide, incl. [tcf-CVil], [tcf-Tepe], [tcf-Zila].

sources.citation: Tiburcio Cano, Gregorio. 2017. La flexión verbal del me'phaa de Zilacayotitlán. MA thesis, CIESAS. 320 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 2.3 'Algunos rasgos fonológicos' pp. 41-63: vowel length contrastive only in monosyllables and the last syllable of polysyllables (citing Suárez 1983:47, Carrasco 2006, Navarro 2012); contour tones in final syllable. No acento/prominence statement.
